skill.name: theater-detection-audit
skill.description: Audits codebases for placeholder behavior such as mock data, TODO markers, stub functions, commented production logic, and simplified error handling. It helps agents inspect context, rank risk, plan completion work, and replace theater with production-ready implementations.
skill.summary: Finds placeholder code and guides production-ready completion work.
skill.author: DNYoussef

content.value_statement: Placeholder code hides product risk and can reach production with fake behavior. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through a structured audit that finds, prioritizes, and replaces theater with real implementations.
actual_capabilities: Scans scoped files for TODO, FIXME, HACK, XXX, TEMP, STUB, MOCK, and similar markers.
Identifies hardcoded responses, mock data, stub functions, commented logic, weak error handling, and test-only paths.
Reads surrounding context to infer intended production behavior and dependencies.
Prioritizes findings by operational risk, user impact, and dependency order.
Produces an audit report with locations, descriptions, completion roadmap, and progress tracking.
Guides replacement work with validation, logging, security, testing, and documentation checks.
limitations: Requires a clear audit scope; very large repositories should be reviewed in phases.
Cannot resolve unclear product requirements without user or stakeholder input.
May flag legitimate test fixtures unless test and production boundaries are clear.
Does not replace a dedicated security, performance, or compliance audit.

use_cases.title: Release Readiness Review
use_cases.description: Find placeholder logic before a release branch moves to production.

use_cases.title: Legacy Code Handoff
use_cases.description: Separate real implementations from mocks when adopting an unfamiliar codebase.

use_cases.title: Prototype Hardening
use_cases.description: Convert rapid prototype shortcuts into tracked, prioritized implementation work.

prompt_templates.title: Find Basic Theater
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner audit of a small folder.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the theater-detection-audit skill on the src folder. Find TODO markers, mock data, stub functions, and hardcoded responses. Summarize each item with file, line, risk, and suggested next step.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare A Release Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the theater-detection-audit skill on the release branch. Focus on user-facing flows, API clients, authentication, payments, and error handling. Produce a prioritized completion roadmap.

prompt_templates.title: Map Theater Dependencies
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate audit where placeholders block each other.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the theater-detection-audit skill to map dependencies between placeholder implementations. Identify which mocks or stubs block other work, then recommend the safest completion order.

prompt_templates.title: Complete High-Risk Theater
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the theater-detection-audit skill to identify high-risk theater, read full context, design production replacements, and list tests that prove the real behavior works.

output_examples.input: Audit src/api before a production release.
output_examples.output: The audit found fixed responses in two API paths, one empty retry handler, and one TODO in payment validation. Payment validation is highest priority because it affects checkout accuracy.

output_examples.input: Review a prototype for mocks that must be replaced.
output_examples.output: The report separates harmless demo fixtures from production blockers. It recommends completing the real data client first because four other placeholders depend on it.

output_examples.input: Check whether completed theater is actually production-ready.
output_examples.output: The review confirms two replacements and flags one weak completion. The remaining item still catches all errors silently and needs observable failure handling.

best_practices: Provide narrow paths, important flows, and release goals before starting the audit.
Review findings with a domain owner before replacing business logic.
Add tests that fail against placeholders and pass against real implementations.
anti_patterns: Running the audit across a huge repository without phase boundaries.
Treating test fixtures as production failures without checking their scope.
Replacing placeholders before confirming requirements, data sources, and failure behavior.

faq.question: What does this skill mean by theater?
faq.answer: Theater means code that appears complete but uses placeholders, mocks, stubs, or simplified behavior.

faq.question: Can it update code after finding placeholders?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow includes designing and implementing production replacements when requirements and dependencies are clear.

faq.question: Does it work with any programming language?
faq.answer: It is language-agnostic, but results depend on clear scope and readable project structure.

faq.question: Will it flag normal tests?
faq.answer: It may flag test fixtures for review, but legitimate test-only code should be separated from production blockers.

faq.question: How should I scope a large audit?
faq.answer: Start with production entry points, critical user flows, and risky integrations. Audit the rest in phases.

faq.question: Is this a security audit?
faq.answer: No. It can surface risky placeholders, but it does not replace dedicated security review.
